To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diurnal behaviour of salivary proteins and amylase activity in patients with diabetes is similar to the behaviour of the same parameters in healthy individuals.

(a) the diurnal behaviour of salivary amylase activity is the same for the diabetic patients as for the control subjects, (b) salivary proteins have the same diurnality for the IDDM and NIDDM patients, and (c) the diurnal pattern of salivary proteins differs for the diabetic patients from the one observed for the control subjects.
the diurnal behaviour of salivary proteins, amylase and density is different in diabetic patients and healthy subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diurnal changes in the salivary parameters of patients with diabetes and the comparison with healthy subjects.
the diurnal behaviour of salivary proteins, amylase and density in patients with diabetes and the comparison of these results with the control subjects.
the study of some diurnal behaviour of salivary parameters (density, amylase and protein concentration) in healthy subjects, in patients with IDDM and NIDDM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diurnal changes of salivary density and amylase activity were similar in diabetic and healthy subjects, whereas those of proteins were different.
salivary density and amylase activity are not altered by diabetes, while salivary proteins are influenced by diabetes.
the diurnal behaviour of salivary parameters is different for the 2 groups of diabetic patients (IDDM and NIDDM) in comparison with the healthy subjects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diurnal behaviour of some parameters in saliva of diabetic subjects is different from that in non-diabetic subjects.
the diurnal behaviour of salivary parameters is different for diabetic patients and healthy individuals.
in diabetic patients the diurnal changes in the salivary parameters are more pronounced than in healthy subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diurnal behaviour of the salivary parameters is not influenced by the diabetes, but by other factors such as age, sex or the type of diabetes.
the salivary proteins have diurnal changes and this could be an important parameter in saliva diagnostics.
the diurnal behaviour of salivary parameters can be different in diabetic patients and healthy individuals.
